review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

13:1.sourceText: Πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἐξουσίαις ὑπερεχούσαις ὑποτασσέσθω. οὐ γὰρ ἔστιν ἐξουσία εἰ μὴ ὑπὸ Θεοῦ, αἱ δὲ οὖσαι ὑπὸ Θεοῦ τεταγμέναι εἰσίν.
13:1.targetText: Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.

groups.note: Πᾶσα ψυχή ("every soul") is rendered Everyone.
The article with the participle, αἱ οὖσαι ("the existing ones"), is rendered The authorities that exist.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and does not render δέ.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the pronoun, relative and copula; the Greek has only ὑπὸ Θεοῦ ("by God").

13:2.sourceText: ὥστε ὁ ἀντιτασσόμενος τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ διαταγῇ ἀνθέστηκεν· οἱ δὲ ἀνθεστηκότες ἑαυτοῖς κρίμα λήμψονται.
13:2.targetText: Consequently, whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.

groups.note: The article τῇ ("the") with διαταγῇ ("ordinance") is rendered what.
The noun διαταγή ("ordinance") is rendered as the clause what God has set in place.
The article with the participle, οἱ ἀνθεστηκότες ("those who have resisted"), is rendered those who do so.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

13:3.sourceText: οἱ γὰρ ἄρχοντες οὐκ εἰσὶν φόβος τῷ ἀγαθῷ ἔργῳ ἀλλὰ τῷ κακῷ. θέλεις δὲ μὴ φοβεῖσθαι τὴν ἐξουσίαν; τὸ ἀγαθὸν ποίει, καὶ ἕξεις ἔπαινον ἐξ αὐτῆς·
13:3.targetText: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority? Then do what is right, and you will have his approval.

groups.note: μὴ φοβεῖσθαι ("not to fear") is rendered to be unafraid of; English has no separate not.
ἐξουσία ("authority") stands for the person who holds it and is rendered one in authority.
The article τό ("the") is rendered what.
ἐξ αὐτῆς ("from it", the authority) is rendered his.

English adds Then to present the command as the answer to the question; the Greek has no connective here.

13:4.sourceText: Θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν σοὶ εἰς τὸ ἀγαθόν. ἐὰν δὲ τὸ κακὸν ποιῇς, φοβοῦ· οὐ γὰρ εἰκῇ τὴν μάχαιραν φορεῖ· Θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν, ἔκδικος εἰς ὀργὴν τῷ τὸ κακὸν πράσσοντι.
13:4.targetText: For he is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword in vain. He is God’s servant, an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer.

groups.note: σοί ("for you") is rendered your.
ἔκδικος ("avenger") is rendered an agent of retribution together with εἰς ὀργήν.
ὀργή ("wrath") is rendered retribution.
The article with the participle, τῷ τὸ κακὸν πράσσοντι ("to the one doing evil"), is rendered to the wrongdoer.

13:5.sourceText: διὸ ἀνάγκη ὑποτάσσεσθαι, οὐ μόνον διὰ τὴν ὀργὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν.
13:5.targetText: Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority, not only to avoid punishment, but also as a matter of conscience.

groups.note: The noun ἀνάγκη ("necessity") is rendered necessary.
ὀργή ("wrath") is rendered punishment.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts the cause διά ("because of") as the purpose to avoid, which has a different meaning.

English supplies the object of submit.
English adds avoid, turning the cause into a purpose; διά means "because of".

13:6.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ φόρους τελεῖτε· λειτουργοὶ γὰρ Θεοῦ εἰσιν εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο προσκαρτεροῦντες.
13:6.targetText: This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.

groups.note: Διὰ τοῦτο ("because of this") is rendered This is why.
αὐτὸ τοῦτο ("this very thing") is rendered work.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB has no word for γάρ here.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds the copula in This is why.
English names the subject that εἰσιν ("they are") gives only by its ending.
English supplies the possessive; αὐτό ("very") agrees with τοῦτο and does not mean their.

13:7.sourceText: ἀπόδοτε πᾶσιν τὰς ὀφειλάς, τῷ τὸν φόρον τὸν φόρον, τῷ τὸ τέλος τὸ τέλος, τῷ τὸν φόβον τὸν φόβον, τῷ τὴν τιμὴν τὴν τιμήν.
13:7.targetText: Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.

groups.note: The article τάς ("the") is rendered what.
The noun ὀφειλάς ("dues") is rendered as the clause what you owe him.
The article τῷ, used as a pronoun ("to the one"), is rendered to whom.

13:8.sourceText: Μηδενὶ μηδὲν ὀφείλετε, εἰ μὴ τὸ ἀλλήλους ἀγαπᾶν· ὁ γὰρ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἕτερον νόμον πεπλήρωκεν.
13:8.targetText: Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

groups.note: The articular infinitive τὸ ἀγαπᾶν ("to love") is rendered in love.
The object ἀλλήλους ("one another") is rendered to one another, in parallel with to no one.
The article τόν has possessive force here.
ἕτερον ("the other") is rendered neighbor.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the object μηδέν ("anything") unexpressed.

13:9.sourceText: τὸ γάρ Οὐ μοιχεύσεις, Οὐ φονεύσεις, Οὐ κλέψεις, Οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις, καὶ εἴ τις ἑτέρα ἐντολή, ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ ἀνακεφαλαιοῦται, ἐν τῷ Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.
13:9.targetText: The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”

groups.note: The neuter article τό introduces the quoted commandments.
A future with οὐ ("you shall not commit adultery") is a prohibition, rendered Do not commit adultery.
Both ἐν ("in") locate the summing up; BSB renders them with one in and introduces the quoted command with a colon, as in Galatians 5:14.
The future Ἀγαπήσεις ("you shall love") is a command, rendered Love.

BSB leaves εἰ ("if") unexpressed: and any other commandments.

13:10.sourceText: ἡ ἀγάπη τῷ πλησίον κακὸν οὐκ ἐργάζεται· πλήρωμα οὖν νόμου ἡ ἀγάπη.
13:10.targetText: Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.

groups.note: The article makes the indeclinable πλησίον ("near") a noun and carries the dative; τῷ πλησίον is rendered to its neighbor.

13:11.sourceText: Καὶ τοῦτο εἰδότες τὸν καιρόν, ὅτι ὥρα ἤδη ὑμᾶς ἐξ ὕπνου ἐγερθῆναι· νῦν γὰρ ἐγγύτερον ἡμῶν ἡ σωτηρία ἢ ὅτε ἐπιστεύσαμεν.
13:11.targetText: And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.

13:12.sourceText: ἡ νὺξ προέκοψεν, ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤγγικεν. ἀποθώμεθα οὖν τὰ ἔργα τοῦ σκότους, ἐνδυσώμεθα δὲ τὰ ὅπλα τοῦ φωτός.
13:12.targetText: The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB joins the clauses with a semicolon and does not render δέ.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

13:13.sourceText: ὡς ἐν ἡμέρᾳ εὐσχημόνως περιπατήσωμεν, μὴ κώμοις καὶ μέθαις, μὴ κοίταις καὶ ἀσελγείαις, μὴ ἔριδι καὶ ζήλῳ·
13:13.targetText: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.

13:14.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἐνδύσασθε τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, καὶ τῆς σαρκὸς πρόνοιαν μὴ ποιεῖσθε εἰς ἐπιθυμίας.
13:14.targetText: Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.
